public_rationale: The evidence makes substantial lab dependence plausible but does not settle the full claim. Bloomberg estimates that OpenAI supplied about 70% of Microsoft’s annual AI sales using an inferred revenue total. That cannot establish the stated threshold across Google, Amazon and Microsoft, or nearly complete compute allocation. CoreWeave’s announcement confirms a lab connection, but a connection alone does not explain realized growth. Alphabet identifies several growth drivers without quantifying their customer shares. Neither the collective nor the individual reading is settled, and no clean counterexample establishes that the universal neocloud claim is false.
limitations: The assessment preserves the fiscal-year example and does not impose a quarter-only test.
Company statements about growth drivers are not independent causal measurements.
Unavailable primary records limit the evidence collected.
The unknown accounting basis prevents a supported or contradicted financial verdict under the stated rules.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: The author believes Google, Amazon and Microsoft, but notably not Meta, have seen remarkable revenue growth in the AI era because they sell effectively all their available compute to Anthropic or OpenAI, which make up more than 70% of their AI revenues. He believes this is also why the only AI data center companies with any revenue growth, such as CoreWeave, Nebius and IREN, are connected directly or by proxy to those two labs.

statement.excerpt: I believe the reason that Google, Amazon, Microsoft, and most notably not Meta have seen remarkable revenue growth in the AI era is that they’re selling effectively all of their available compute to either Anthropic or OpenAI, who make up more than 70% of their AI revenues

from_speaker: Google, Amazon, Microsoft, and most notably not Meta
remarkable revenue growth in the AI era
selling effectively all of their available compute to either Anthropic or OpenAI
more than 70% of their AI revenues
the only AI data center companies with any revenue growth
connected directly or by proxy to the two AI labs
our_interpretation: The ordinary reading is that purchases by the two labs largely explain the named providers’ growth. 'I believe' expresses confidence in this checkable explanation; it is not a conditional antecedent.

In the surrounding discussion, 'available compute' means available AI compute offered to customers. 'Effectively all' means nearly all, allowing a small remainder; the author supplies no exact allocation threshold.

The words do not settle whether the greater-than-70% threshold applies collectively or separately to Google, Amazon and Microsoft. Examine both readings where possible. A result that depends on choosing between them must be flagged.

The period is the AI era through publication, with no explicit starting date. The nearby Microsoft example concerns its most recent fiscal year. Retain that annual comparison and do not restrict the entire claim to April–June 2026.
Read Meta’s exclusion as an exception to the proposed compute-sales explanation, rather than an independent assertion that Meta had no revenue growth.
A connection by proxy means an identifiable commercial chain supplying the labs. Mere participation in the same technology industry does not establish such a connection.

The supplied passage does not identify the accounting or estimation basis for the cross-company AI revenue share. It is recorded as unknown, rather than assigning the basis of a subsequently found source.
criteria.support_condition: Comparable customer revenue and capacity records show that the two labs account for more than 70% of AI revenue under the applicable reading, buy nearly all available AI compute, and largely explain the named providers’ growth. Records also establish the asserted commercial connections among growing AI data center providers. Connections and concentration alone are insufficient to establish the causal explanation.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Comparable records materially refute the asserted concentration or near-total compute allocation, show that the proposed mechanism does not largely explain the growth, or identify a growing AI data center provider without the asserted direct or proxy commercial connection. A provider-level share below 70% alone does not refute the collective reading. Other customers’ existence alone does not refute 'effectively all.'

evidence.explanation: Bloomberg estimates that OpenAI supplied about 70% of Microsoft’s fiscal-year AI sales, using an inferred annual AI revenue total. This supports the plausibility of substantial concentration at Microsoft, but does not establish a greater-than-70% share across the three providers, near-total compute allocation, or causation; the press estimate is used because a complete primary customer-share calculation was not obtained.

evidence.locator: Anat Ashkenazi’s prepared remarks, Google Cloud segment
evidence.explanation: Alphabet identifies several contributors to Cloud growth. This is material context against attributing growth predominantly to lab compute purchases, but the statement supplies neither customer revenue shares nor quantified causal contributions.

evidence.excerpt: The multi-year agreement will bring compute online starting later this year.
evidence.explanation: The announcement confirms CoreWeave’s direct commercial connection to Anthropic. Its prospective delivery language does not establish that this agreement generated the revenue growth already observed.

evidence.locator: Customer-list paragraph following “Today, Runpod counts 500,000 developers”
evidence.explanation: The report identifies a broad customer list that also includes OpenAI. Runpod therefore does not provide a clean counterexample to the connection claim, and the list does not establish dependence or revenue concentration.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: Comparable realized customer revenue and AI revenue totals, dated compute allocation records, and evidence tracing growth to lab purchases would resolve the central explanation. A documented growing AI data center provider without a relevant lab connection could resolve the universal component against the claim.
